messages:
Evelyn Tran: quick flag 1: saved views' quota/cost preview is misleading when routing policies change model at runtime. users expect the saved view preview to reflect what will actually run.
Samir Rao: can you show an example?
Evelyn Tran: user saves view on Route X with predicate model=="rwd-7b-q4" and preview shows 0.8 tokens/sec cost. but when Route X is routed to fallback model rwd-3b due to capacity, the actual token burn is different and the console still shows the original preview.
Lina M: that's bad. the console should either: 1) compute preview using routing policy simulation or 2) show a small badge: "preview assumes pinned model" vs "preview uses effective routing".
Denise (product): UX tradeoff: simulating routing on every hover might be expensive. can we cache a simulation or do an on-demand validate?
Samir Rao: backend side we already compute routing plan at request time. propose adding a lightweight endpoint `/saved_views/:id/estimate?target_route=...&respect_routing=true` that returns the effective model and quota estimate.
Evelyn Tran: nice. what would the contract look like?
Samir Rao: pseudo-response:
```json
{
  "view_id": "sv_01F...",
  "requested_scope": "route",
  "requested_predicates": ["latency > 300", "model == \"rwd-7b-q4\""],
  "effective_model": "rwd-3b",
  "compatibility": "model_routed",
  "quota_estimate": "0.42_tokens_per_min",
  "notes": ["routed due to capacity policy: fallback_low_latency"]
}
```
Lina M: small naming nit: use snake_case in API? we've been inconsistent. also `quota_estimate` should include units and sample window, e.g., `{value, unit, window}` or a single string is ambiguous.
Denise (product): agree on structured fields. but remember file-level schema constraints for saved views. maybe add `estimate_meta: "v1"` for future-proofing.
Samir Rao: good call. I'll make it `{value: "0.42", unit: "tokens_per_min", window: "1m"}` in the next PR.
qa-bot: reminder: console-api deploy freeze is Fri 02:00 UTC. any incompatible API changes must go through migration plan.
Evelyn Tran: migration concerns: existing saved views that reference models might be silently mismatched after we start returning effective_model. we should annotate legacy saved views with `legacy_routing_annotation` via a backfill job.
Lina M: also we need a frontend affordance: when user opens a saved view, show a compact banner: "This view will run on rwd-3b due to routing policy (was saved with rwd-7b-q4). Preview updated" with an option: "Show original preview".
Denise (product): telemetry ask: capture `saved_view.preview_simulated` with tags { view_id, original_model, effective_model, compatibility, preview_source } and sample at 5% to start. want to measure how often preview differs from actual run.
Samir Rao: backend will emit an event when `/estimate` returns compatibility != "ok". we can surface that to metrics too.
Evelyn Tran: follow-ups: 1) Samir to spec API + compatibility enum 2) Lina to prototype banner copy + "Show original" button 3) Data/backfill ticket to flag legacy views 4) Denise to own telemetry schema. I'll create tickets and assign.
Lina M: also q: should the saved view editor include a toggle "Respect routing policies for previews"? might be useful for power users.
Denise (product): default to ON but remember to persist user preference in console settings.
Samir Rao: I'll start the PR but will stub the estimate endpoint under a feature flag. ping me for API enum names.
Evelyn Tran: thanks all. small follow-up: can the UI call `/saved_views/:id/estimate` on hover and fall back to cached value if flagged rate-limited? keep calls cheap.
Samir Rao: yes we'll gate it and throttle by user/session.
Denise (product): marking actionable items in product board now. :white_check_mark:
